description: Everything after 12:23 PM MDT on September 10, 2025 — the surrender chain, the courtyard being paved over, gag orders, media fights, TPUSA and law-enforcement resignations, the trial, the memorial, and visa enforcement.

AmericaFest, TPUSA's flagship Phoenix conference and the stage that recurs most in this case — speaker fights, the July 2025 anchor week, the August 25 flyer, the Candace Owens invitation, and the first AmFest without Charlie Kirk.
Cross-cutting analysis and documentation pages for the investigation — synthesized write-ups that sit above any single evidence thread rather than covering one topic.
Pre-September 10 context for the UVU event — donor meetings, reported death-warning texts, recon-pattern searches, aircraft movements, the possible Fort Huachuca meeting week, and UVU GRAMA warnings.

Every camera thread in the case — UVU CCTV, Ring and WYZE doorbell footage, mobile eyewitness video, TPUSA production cameras, merchant CCTV, and the disputed handling of cameras and SD cards at the scene.
Utah Valley University and the wider higher-education response — campus policy, university statements, security posture, and how other institutions reacted to the assassination.

What actually killed Charlie Kirk. Citizen investigators conclude an explosive device — most likely in the microphone — rather than the .30-06 rifle round of the official account. The site's central evidentiary question.
Suppression of speech about the assassination — X account bans, deleted eyewitness video, court gag orders, TPUSA legal threats, and platform scrubbing of investigation material.
Charlie Kirk himself — biography, beliefs, his Israel and Iran-war positions, donor friction, reported warnings he received, and why he was the target. The victim and motive anchor of the case.

Master index of every company, LLC, non-profit, PAC, and government body profiled in the investigation — private security firms, TPUSA entities, U.S. agencies, and foreign government and intelligence bodies.

Consciousness-control claims bearing on the case — Havana Syndrome, Voice of God and V2K, directed-energy effects, brain-to-brain research, and why an intelligence service would want a shooter who looks unstable.

State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson, case 251403576 — judges, prosecution and defense teams, discovery fights, gag orders, preliminary hearing transcripts, ballistics disputes, and Miranda-timing motions.

Cover-up claims: rapid alteration of the crime scene, withheld records, deleted eyewitness footage, halted foreign-lead inquiries, gag orders, and narrative control. Framed as attributed hypotheses, not proven findings.
Defamation lawsuits arising out of the case — witnesses, security figures, and commentators suing each other, and where civil discovery in those suits could force case facts into the open.
Figures who pulled police, scanners, and cameras toward false leads at UVU — George Zinn, early patsies, crew members near the tent, and people still unidentified. Most were cleared or released.
Reported and claimed drone activity around UVU — military ISR platforms, TPUSA B-roll aerials, weaponized-UAS theories, and the disclosure gaps about what was airborne over the campus that day.

The B-Field Resonant Cascade hypothesis — an unverified citizen theory that a pulsed electromagnetic discharge through the corded microphone at a prepared resonant site, not a rifle round, killed Charlie Kirk.

The FBI's role — federal posture over a state case, ballistics stewardship and the banned CBLA test, witness coordination, press briefings, blocking of other agencies' inquiries, and the open transparency questions.

The four proposed federal disclosure laws modeled on the Epstein Files Transparency Act — the reform path this site argues is how the truth actually gets forced out. Public card layout plus each law's full text.

Google Trends claims of pre-September 10 search interest in case people, places, planes, and institutions from Israel, Washington D.C., and federal corridors. Leads only — Trends cannot show who searched or why.
How government entities handled the physical and documentary evidence — chain of custody, records retention, and the claims about what was altered, withheld, or never collected.

Government behavioral-control programs against the Tyler Robinson patsy and handler theories — MKUltra, Project Artichoke, V2K, platform radicalization, and intelligence tradecraft for manufacturing a lone gunman.
Reference map of the government agencies appearing in the case — federal, state, and local — describing what each does and where it touches the investigation, without adjudicating any of them.

Weapon and ammunition analysis — the Mauser Model 98 .30-06 narrative, the ATF inconclusive match, energy and trajectory problems, acoustic direction, and why the wound does not fit the claimed round.
The independent podcasters, X researchers, and YouTube creators actually driving this investigation — who is trusted, what each broke, and the censorship pressure they came under.
Foreign intelligence threads — Israeli phones clustered at UVU, Egyptian jets, Mossad capability and motive claims, OSINT search patterns, and the halted NCTC review of foreign ties.
Iran did not kill Charlie Kirk, but his public opposition to a U.S. war with Iran put him against that war's most powerful advocates. Mapped as reported motive claims, not proven fact.

Israel, Israeli policy debate, and pro-Israel donor and advocacy networks as they appear in Charlie Kirk's life and death — the funding pressure, the public fights, and the friction in his final months.

Why reporting and citizen investigators name Israel and Mossad as the leading suspect — motive, Israeli presence at UVU, the Iran war push, influence over TPUSA, and the shutdown of foreign-involvement leads.
Investigative roster of everyone peripheral to the killing, organized by role, linking each name out to its People profile and to the case threads that person appears in.
Who actually killed Charlie Kirk — the competing theories investigators are pursuing, and what evidence each rests on. The section that states the alternatives to the official lone-shooter account.
Non-FBI government police and prosecutors — UVU campus police, Orem PD, Utah county sheriffs, DPS, plus crime-scene handling, the manhunt, the arrest sequence, and the state prosecution.

The four federal forced-disclosure laws in full drafting detail — DoJ/FBI disclosure, U.S. intelligence disclosure, mandating the investigation, and trusted investigators — with the discovery list behind each.
The legal dimension broadly — court proceedings, evidence handling, gag orders, and the legal investigation into the September 10, 2025 UVU shooting.
Legal proceedings and evidence handling as a process — how records were requested, sealed, produced, or refused, and what the legal machinery has and has not disclosed.
Hyperlinked index of every key place in the case — the UVU courtyard and Losee Center roof, the custody chain, airports, hospitals, courts, the staging house, and disputed property leads.
Maps and spatial analysis — the UVU campus geometry, sight lines from the claimed firing position, travel routes, and the geographic reasoning behind trajectory and movement claims.

How newspapers, broadcast TV, and digital platforms covered the assassination and the Robinson capital case — framing choices, the early 'shot to the heart' description, censorship, and trial press access.

Medical and forensic questions — the wound itself, fragments, the Timpanogos hospital transport, the sealed autopsy, the medical examiner report signature dispute, and conflicting witness accounts of the injury.

The likely Fort Huachuca meeting of September 9, 2025 — possibly September 8 — the day before the assassination. HARD RULE: never list any attendee or likely attendee names. Readers are pointed to open-source search terms instead.
Every reported message Charlie Kirk sent or received in the weeks before September 10, 2025 — one page per message, with its source, its channel, and its verification status.
The exploding-mic theory — video and Canon XA55 audio evidence, RODE hardware and its DoD contract, AES procurement, the burnt fragment in the SUV, the AV team, and mic-over-versus-under placement.

Why Charlie Kirk was killed — donor and Israel pressure, the Iran war, reported death warnings, geopolitical intelligence context, TPUSA internal dynamics, and the motives alleged against Tyler Robinson.
How the story was framed in real time — the 'shot to the heart' description, the wrong-guy and confession framings, media amplification, and the narratives that appeared and then quietly receded.
Organizations and groups connected to the case beyond the main corporate and government index — advocacy bodies, campus groups, and networks that appear in the record.
Cross-cutting topics spanning multiple sections — investigation methodology, miscellaneous evidence leads, and public response.
Additional topics and analysis that do not fit the main sections but belong in the investigation record.
Profiles of every individual connected to the assassination — the victim, the accused, family members, witnesses, security personnel, officials, and investigators. The site's person-lookup hub.
Photographic evidence — official and media images, crime-scene stills, comparison photos, and the per-image Level 5 pages generated from the image pipeline.

Aircraft and flight-path evidence — the planes that repeatedly appeared near Charlie Kirk's speaking events, SAM military flights, Egyptian jets, N1098L, erased ADS-B records, and the recovery of that deleted data.
The political environment surrounding the assassination — the Iran war fight, the 2025 political landscape, and the consequences of the killing for the movement Charlie Kirk built.

The indicators pointing to intelligence-service involvement at UVU — the halted NCTC inquiry, clustered NSA-detectable phones, HADES flights, Egyptian jets, federal-signature behaviors, and the Israel motive.

Evidence and argument that Tyler Robinson did not cause Charlie Kirk's death — ATF ballistics, wound and trajectory mismatch, acoustics, identity gaps, clothing conflicts, and timeline contradictions.

The Losee Center roof, the alleged firing position — the run and military-style crawl, black clothing versus jeans, screwdriver and helicopter disputes, muzzle-flash claims, and who the roof figure actually was.
Legacy hub, now split — the private Security Team that guarded Charlie Kirk on one side and the government Law Enforcement agencies on the other. Kept as a pointer to both.
The private protective detail responsible for Charlie Kirk at UVU — the contracted firm, the individuals on the detail, and the reported failures in the protection plan that day.
Analysis of online posts, platform behavior, and digital evidence — account activity, post timing and deletions, and what the social record shows around September 10, 2025.
Alternative suspects and persons of interest beyond Tyler Robinson — dispatch audio leads, the grey van laser report, construction-site witnesses, and competing shooter-location theories.

What citizen investigators flag as suspicious, sorted by actor: state and local law enforcement, the FBI, an alleged Israeli nexus, U.S. intelligence, and the defense. Attributed claims, not proven findings.
Technical and surveillance evidence — drones, signals capability, data centers, device tracking, and the technology questions that bear on who could have done this and who could see it.
The event tent and courtyard beneath Charlie Kirk — paving contractors, state earth-moving crews, how fast the site was altered afterward, and inside-the-tent device and shooter theories.
High-level map of every major theory about what happened, what each claims, and what supports or undercuts it. The routing page that sends readers into the section arguing each one.
Chronological hub — 2024 signals, the 2025 pre-shot arc, the September 10 day-of sequence, the surrender chain, witness-account gaps, and the post-shot milestones.
Long-form analytical essays cutting across the case — ballistics and surveillance claims, pre-assassination context, the September 10 event timeline, and the political aftermath.
Detailed analysis and documentation across assorted aspects of the investigation that were organized as a third topic tier.

Turning Point USA — its structure, funding, donor influence, and internal dynamics; the staff and AV crew present at UVU; and the questions raised by the organization's conduct after Charlie Kirk's death.
The official suspect — identity mismatches, the surrender timeline, the Discord confession, ballistics, Miranda timing, his family, his trial, and the patsy theories. He is charged, not convicted.

Why the reported case against Tyler Robinson fails — the .30-06 wound mismatch, an exploding-mic kill mechanism, a Discord confession that appears fabricated, and the cover-up indicators around his arrest.
U.S. intelligence community threads — the NCTC foreign-ties review that was ordered stopped, NSA Bumblehive phone collection, CIA campus links, and Fort Huachuca timing the week of the assassination.

The reported reasons U.S. intelligence assisted in the death — the RODE microphone and its DoD contract, the AES factory explosion and deaths, narrative control, Fort Huachuca, a faked confession, and the cover-up.

Utah Valley University as the physical setting — the Orem campus, the courtyard layout, the Losee Center, event permitting and setup, campus security decisions, and the university's records and responses.
Video evidence and analysis — the official production feed, eyewitness phone footage, broadcast aerials, frame-by-frame breakdowns, and the per-video Level 5 pages generated from the video pipeline.
How citizens respond through voting and civic engagement — which offices and votes actually bear on forcing disclosure in this case.
Firsthand accounts from people at UVU on September 10, 2025 — on-camera and written testimony, what each witness described, and where their accounts conflict with the official narrative.
Concrete actions an individual can take — contacting representatives about the four laws, filing records requests, preserving evidence, spreading findings, and pressing for a real investigation.
